subject: wizardBookshelf
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: wizard's bookshelf with tomes, scrolls, orbs and candles.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm planning the TypeScript module structure, deciding to add a simple root joint at the origin even though this prop may not strictly need joints, then sketching out the design concept of a tall, ornate dark wood wizard's bookshelf.

I'm figuring out all the details: gold trim, arched crescent-moon crown, four shelves stocked with colorful tomes, scrolls, a crystal ball, a floating orb, melted candles with glowing flames, a hanging lantern, and a rune-etched plinth rug underneath, all rendered in a toon/cel-shaded anime style using the glow kit for lighting effects. Now I'm working out exact dimensions—roughly 1.5m wide, 0.42m deep, with the cabinet body rising to 2.0m and the arched crown peaking at 2.45m—and planning the coordinate layout centered on the x-axis, starting with the base plinth and rug dimensions before building the shelf geometry upward.

I'll close in the bottom section as a cabinet with two doors, gold trim, a round moon emblem decal, and a knob, then stack three open shelf compartments above at roughly even heights up to the top.

Settling on levels 0.66, 1.18, 1.70, 2.22 for consistent 0.48 free-height compartments, with the cabinet base at 0.14 to 0.66. For the crown above the top board, I'm designing a pointed pediment arch spanning the width with a peak rising 0.38 above, topped with a glowing crescent moon and stars.

Total height comes out around 2.7-2.9m which is tall but fitting for a wizard's shelf, so I'll scale the crown down slightly to 0.32 to keep things proportional against a 1.5m width. For the back panel, I'm planning a dark blue painted board with a starry night-sky texture, possibly one large plane spanning across the compartments rather than separate pieces.

Now I'm thinking about the side panels with gold trim strips and carved rune decals, plus lathe-turned gilt columns at the front corners with spiral or ring-band detailing to give the shelf an ornate, ceremonial look.

For books, I'm designing a helper function that builds each book as a cover box with an inset cream page block, positioning the spine facing forward and hiding the fore-edge pages at the back, keeping dimensions proportional for thickness, height, and depth.

Each book comes out to roughly 7 parts (spine, two boards, pages, bands, label), so 30 books would total around 210 parts -- I need to check whether that stays within my overall part budget of 340 once other furniture elements are added.

I'm reconsidering the structure to cut part count: maybe around 24 books with simpler builds -- a single cover box plus a pages box, or three boxes for spine/boards plus pages, skipping individual bands in favor of a texture applied to the spine surface.

A transparent overlay plane sits just in front of the spine with gold bands, label, and rune drawn into the texture, giving 3-4 reusable variations across books. That brings each book down to five parts total -- spine, two boards, pages, and the decal overlay -- accepting some stretching of the ornament pattern as a fair tradeoff.

For leaning books, I'm defining a placement helper that takes a base point and quaternion, computing each part's world position by applying a Z-axis rotation (for lean) to its local offset before adding it to the base, so tilted stacks can be built without reworking the box geometry itself.

For books lying flat, I'm switching to a center-based placement function instead, using a 90° rotation about Z to reorient the height axis onto the x-axis, which lets me reuse the same book builder for both standing and horizontal books by just swapping the quaternion and center point.

Adding spine overlay plane...

Estimating paint texel density across the shelf scene — maybe 20-30 m² of painted area, giving roughly 5mm precision which is fine for books and small details. I'll reserve cel-shaded painting for larger surfaces like wood, rug, and stone, using flat colors for small items like books (keeping within the 64-color limit, about 10 distinct book colors). I'm also considering combining wood grain with cel shading for the texture.

Still writing wood and gold materials...

Now I'm planning out the texture list, aiming for 5-12 items: a starry-night back panel, spine overlay variations, a rune-circle rug, a moon-and-star door emblem decal, a hanging scroll with a writing texture, and a crystal ball with a glowing swirl inside.

I'm also considering crescent and star decorations with glow, sparkle-textured floating particle cards, and whether to add extras like a skull candle, hourglass with glowing sand, or potion bottle with glowing liquid, trying to balance richness against budget constraints.

Now I'm working out the precise compartment geometry — defining the inner cabinet dimensions, placing books at the correct depth relative to the front edge, and laying out the cabinet doors with their exact widths and positions within the shelf frame.

For the doors, I'm planning gold-trimmed panels with emblem textures rather than modeled frame geometry — a crescent moon motif on the left door and a sun motif on the right, drawn as textures with ornate borders, plus small gold sphere handles. Then I'm moving into the next compartment's layout, starting with a row of items along its left side.

Working out shelf contents now: the first shelf gets standing books on the left, a crystal ball on a gilt tripod stand in the middle, and a scroll bundle with a candle on the right. The second shelf starts with a stack of flat books topped by a candlestick on the left, followed by more standing books.

Continuing down, I'm filling in the next shelf with a leaning pair of books, an hourglass, a potion bottle, and tilted books resting on a hanging bookend, plus a basket of vertical scroll cylinders further along. For the third shelf, I'm placing a purple orb on a pedestal, an open glowing tome on a lectern in the center, and books with a candelabra on the right, and I'm considering whether a floating orb or ring should hover above this shelf. For the top compartment, I'm thinking a skull with a candle on one side, a stack of books with a hovering glowing orb in the middle, and a scroll tube rack on the other side, though I need to double check I haven't reused any elements already placed.

Now I'm straightening out the level numbering — boards sit at four heights with shelf tops slightly above each, giving three compartments of equal clearance above the cabinet, and I'm setting up a helper constant to offset all these heights consistently. I'm also considering adding an external touch, like a long unrolled scroll drooping down from the front edge of one of the shelf boards for extra visual interest.

Instead of the hanging scroll, I'm leaning toward floor-standing clutter flanking the dais-mounted shelf: a stack of books with a melting candle on the left side, and a cluster of three different-height candles sitting in a wax puddle on the right, using the leftover space on either side of the shelf's footprint on the wider dais.

Now I'm sizing the dais itself, deciding to shift its center forward a bit so there's extra room in front for the rug, and thinking through a reusable candle-building helper that constructs a cylindrical body with drips, a melted wax cap, a thin wick, and a teardrop flame shape for each candle instance.

Writing candle flame geometry...

Estimating about 7 parts per candle across roughly 8 candles gives ~56 parts total, well within budget, so I'm keeping the file around 600-800 lines for efficiency. I'm figuring out the part-building API: each part needs a bone, but with a single root joint, parts default to the nearest joint without needing explicit assignment.

For geometry orientation, cylinders default to the y-axis which works fine, and lathe shapes (for stands, columns, orb bases) use an outline profile with x≥0, also along the default y-axis. For crystal balls, I'm using a low-poly sphere with a swirled purple texture (radial gradients, sparkle lines) to get a glowing magical orb effect, and pairing it with a gilt lathe-profile base shaped like a cupped stand with three feet.

For the floating orb in C3, I'm adding a small glowing cyan sphere encircled by thin gilt torus rings tilted at an angle using rotation offsets to create an orbiting halo effect. For the open tome on the lectern, I'm building an angled box stand with two tilted page slabs in a V shape, book covers beneath, and a glowing textured plane above the pages to represent magical runes.

I'll also add a few floating sparkle cards of runes, then design a scroll helper combining a parchment cylinder body, wooden dowel end caps, a ribbon band, and a wax seal disc, oriented along an axis using a direction parameter.

For the scroll rack, instead of individual holders I like the idea of a "scroll urn" — a lathed vase with 5 scrolls of varying heights standing inside, some with ribbons, tilted naturally for visual interest, keeping the part count efficient.

For extra wow factor I'm adding glowing particle effects and tinted card meshes using the glow helper, and sketching out a gothic-arch crown shape by computing a curved dome outline point-by-point with an elliptical peak.

Actually I'm refining it into a sharper pointed arch using a power curve so it peaks sharply at the center, then extruding that outline into a thin flat shape oriented along the z-axis for the crown's thickness.

Now I'm planning the decorative details: a gold trim sweep following the arch outline slightly offset forward, and a crescent moon shape on the peak made by combining an outer circle arc with an offset inner circle to carve out the crescent silhouette.

Computing inner radius and arc angles...

I'm planning to extrude the crescent with a slight thickness and bevel, giving it a gilded glow, and adding a small glowing star beside it. I'm thinking of placing the crescent as a finial right at the crown's peak, maybe even styling it like it's cradling a glowing orb for a cuter finished look.

Now I'm adding scattered gold mini-stars across the crown face, plus a central circular rune emblem decal glowing at the front, possibly reusing the same rune-circle texture for the rug.

I'm tallying up the texture count — sky, spines, door moon/sun, rug, crown rune, scroll, rune page, orb swirl, sparkle, floor circle — landing around thirteen, a bit over budget but acceptable. I'm deciding to merge a few duplicates and drop the separate hanging-scroll texture, reusing the rune-page texture for it instead to keep things manageable.

Now I'm sizing the texture atlas, giving spines smaller resolution and reserving larger sizes for doors, rug, and sky backgrounds. I'm also working out pillar placement, positioning lathe columns at the front corners of the side panels with specific radius and height offsets so they protrude correctly from the structure.

I'm detailing the lathe column profile with a plinth base, shaft, decorative rings, and capital, using low segment counts for efficiency, then adding a finial spike with a glowing orb at each pillar top for a decorative crown effect. I'm also considering gold trim strips on the outer side panels, deciding to skip rune decals and side details since the camera mostly sees the front, and moving on to cabinet details like the plinth skirting base box.

Now I'm adding gold bottom trim and considering small gold feet at the base corners, then gold trim strips along each shelf's front edge with occasional small gem spheres for accent, while skipping corbel brackets and scalloped trim to keep things simple.

Shifting focus, I'm planning the book spines: defining arrays per shelf specifying thickness, height, depth, color index, texture, and lean, then writing a helper function that places books left to right with small gaps and returns the ending x position. I'm setting up a seeded random generator to vary book placement and selecting a saturated anime-style color palette for the spines, starting with a deep crimson tone.

Adding label rect with rune lines and gem circle, plus a couple ornament variations in gold, cream, and ink tones. Now I'm counting up the books across each cabinet and the floor pile to estimate total parts needed—roughly 30 books at 5 parts each, around 150 pieces total.

Writing book-building function... defining spine, side covers, and page block geometry with placement and rotation logic.

Deciding the pages height should inset 8mm from top and bottom, leaving the boards visibly framing the edges, and placing a thin overlay plane for the cover texture slightly offset to avoid z-fighting. I'm skipping extras like metal corner caps or ribbon bookmarks for now to keep things simple.

For the orb-on-stand helper, I'm planning a lathe-based gilt cup stand with a sphere sitting above it, using modest polygon counts for a low-poly but smooth look, and generating shared swirl textures for a couple of orb color variants to keep texture count reasonable. Starting to think through the hourglass shape using a lathe geometry next.

Simplifying: split hourglass into an upper pale glass lathe shape and a lower lathe shape that glows soft amber to represent the sand, with gilt posts connecting them. For the potion, I'm building a lathe bottle profile with a green glow, plus a brown cork and a small label plane.

For variety I'll add a second bottle in pink alongside the green one, each with cork and ribbon. The skull candle prop gets a cranium sphere, separate jaw box, two dark eye sockets with a faint purple glow, and a small nasal cone, topped with a tall melted candle -- five parts total, placed on the left. I'm skipping the cauldron idea and moving to floor props: a pile of four books with varying yaw plus a tall candle on the left, and a cluster of three candles on the right.

Right side gets a stone saucer holding three candles of varying heights with wax puddle drips and a sparkle, plus a cluster of three tilted spike-shaped crystals glowing cyan nearby as a "mana crystal" accent.

Finishing the crystal placement, then I'm working out the dais itself: a stone box platform with a rug plane on top, and figuring out how the box's UV orientation maps the rug texture correctly on the top face.

Confirmed the rotation math checks out—top faces -z, matching the box orientation. I'll use a plane with the rug texture sitting atop a thin solid-color box for the base, positioned slightly above it. Now I'm sketching the rug's SVG design: a 200x100 viewBox with a burgundy base, gold border, indigo inner field, and a centered circular pattern.

Working out where the magic circle sits relative to the shelf so it isn't fully hidden—shifting the rug's center forward in z, and repositioning the circle lower in the SVG coordinates so its visible radius extends into the area not covered by the shelf's front edge.

Now I'm aligning the rug with the dais footprint, picking consistent width/depth/center values so the rug sits properly inside the platform, then recomputing the circle's z-position and radius against those new rug coordinates. With that settled, I'm starting to figure out the floor height for props resting on the rug, stacking the dais and rug thicknesses to get the final surface level.

Now I'm working out the compartment geometry: board positions spanning the inner width, depth from back panel to front trim, and the side panel boxes running the full cabinet height. I'm placing the back panel plane to cover the span between the cabinet top and the shelf section, computing its vertical center accordingly.

For the back panel texture, I'm setting up a viewBox matching its real-world aspect ratio so I can draw a deep indigo gradient background with small, non-glowing star dots and a few gold constellation lines plus a faint crescent.

Now for the cabinet I'm placing symmetric door panels with a gap, an emblem plate, gold sphere handles, and hinge details, plus front pillars flanking the doors. Starting the helper code with a vector constructor function...

Defining box and cylinder builders...

I'm working out how to batch sparkle cards efficiently—grouping frames by color so each distinct tint only needs one mesh call, since the card's face direction follows the "flow" vector and glow needs a standard material to tint the grayscale texture properly.

For the flame, I'm using a lathe-based teardrop shape oriented along the default y-axis, and for wax drips I'm sketching thin tapered cylinders positioned along the candle's radius to suggest dripping wax.

I'm defining a candle builder function taking position, height, radius, color, flame flag, and tilt, returning the top y-coordinate. Each candle assembles body, rim, wick, inner/outer flame glow, two drips, and a sparkle—about 8 parts each—and I'm planning around seven candles total across shelves and floor clusters.

Now I'm setting up a candlestick holder with a gilt lathe shape and dish, plus a glow function for flame intensity, then moving to book placement logic for the shelves—computing each book's center position, accounting for leaning angles that tilt books about their base and shift their x-offset based on height and thickness.

Still working out lean geometry...

By symmetry I derive a unified sign-based formula using s = sign(a) so the center offset works for both leaning directions, with rotation applied as −a, and now I'm starting to sketch an example layout for the row.

For the last book leaning against its neighbor, I realize leaning toward −x would actually penetrate the neighbor's face, so the correct setup has it leaning toward +x instead, resting against the neighbor to its right rather than left.

So the contact point depends on which wall or panel the leaner rests against: leaning toward the right wall means the top corner touches the panel, giving xc = wallX − h sin a, and similarly for leaning left against the left wall. I'll apply this to place a couple of leaning books in some compartments alongside the vertical stacks, then move on to actually writing out the shelf contents.

Now I'm defining the vertical positions for each shelf level and working out the exact front-to-back placement of books based on their depth, so I can start specifying book rows compartment by compartment with concrete coordinates — starting with the top compartment and listing left-wall leaning books, standing stacks, and their positions.

I'm working through the geometry of leaning books more carefully: figuring out which corner of a tilted book actually touches its neighbor depends on which direction it leans, and I realize my first guess had the lean direction backwards since it would cause an intrusion into the adjacent book rather than a proper contact point.

Thinking of it like a ladder leaning against a wall helps: the book's bottom edge contacts the floor at one corner while the top touches the wall, so I can work out which corner by applying the clockwise rotation formulas to the local coordinates of each corner.

Now checking the mirror case: leaning toward −x works similarly, with the bottom-left corner touching the floor and the top-left corner contacting the neighboring book's right face at x_n. This confirms the general formula for center.x using sign(a) to handle both leaning directions symmetrically.

For a row of books where several lean the same direction against the last vertical book, I need to space consecutive leaners apart by t/cos|a| along x so their contact corners don't overlap. I'm thinking through how to structure this as two helper functions — one for placing vertical books, one for placing a chain of leaning books against a neighbor.

Still defining book specs and color arrays...

Continuing to place objects: a leaning staff ending around -0.1, then a crystal ball on a stand near x=0.12, and a pyramid of lying scrolls centered around x=0.46 to fill out the right side of the shelf.

Actually I'm reconsidering the scroll orientation — better to show them lengthwise along z so we see the circular ends from the front, like a cubbyhole of rolled parchment with visible rod, cap, and optional colored ribbon bands (red, blue, gold) near the front edge, varying the parchment tones between cream and tan for the six scrolls.

For the crystal ball, I'll give it a lathed stand plus sparkle highlights, and I'm thinking of placing a candle to the right atop a small stack of two books near a pyramid of scrolls, working out positions so the pyramid sits centered with evenly spaced rows and the candle stack offset further right.

For the second column I'm laying out a mix of lying book stacks with varying widths and yaw angles, a candlestick with holder dish, several upright books, an hourglass, a pair of potion bottles, and another run of upright books spanning the rest of the row—checking that each element's width keeps the whole arrangement within the frame edges.

For the third column I'm placing a skull with a candle at the far left, then a run of upright books, followed by an open tome in the middle whose spread just touches the previous books without overlapping, and above it I'm adding a glowing rune card and a small floating cyan orb.

Then I'm continuing the right side: a scroll urn with poking scrolls, then a leaning book with a purple orb on a stand nearby. I'm also adding two small hanging star charms dangling from thin gold rods off the shelf underside, giving the scene some whimsical vertical detail.

Writing star outline code...

I'm testing exponent values for the curve profile to get a pointed rather than rounded crown peak, checking derivatives at the center to settle on something closer to a linear triangular taper.

Instead I'll go with a concave tent shape using (1-u)^1.5, steep near the peak and flattening toward the base — giving a wizard-hat brim feel rather than a soft dome.

For the crown trim, I'm tracing the outline slightly inset from the roof edge, using an exact polyline through the same curve points rather than a catmull spline so the peak stays sharp instead of rounding off.

I also need an eave trim box along the bottom edge, plus a front emblem: a glowing circular plane centered above the eaves, textured with a dark navy disc and bright cyan/gold rune strokes so the glow reads against the dark fill.

For the peak, I'm adding a gilt crescent moon finial with a small orb nested in its mouth and a short stem, placing it so the total structure height comes out around 2.9 units. I also want small spire finials with orbs at the crown corners, positioned above the pillar tops near x=±0.76/±0.78.

Now I'm working out the pillar lathe profile, figuring the pillar should sit on top of the 0.14-tall base plinth and extend up to the crown height, with the plinth itself slightly wider than the pillar spacing so the pillars touch its edge.

Defining the lathe outline with ring bands and capital...

I'm setting up a paint function for the pillar that colors ring zones gold and the rest wood, then moving on to the SVG texture strings, starting with the sky texture.

Writing the sky gradient and stars...

Still writing spine overlay designs... I'm also realizing the plane's stretched aspect ratio versus the SVG's native proportions could distort the ornaments vertically by 2-3x, so I need to account for that when positioning bands and gems.

Now I'm planning the door emblem designs at a 120x84 viewBox with gold frame strokes and corner flourishes, sized so stroke widths stay visibly thick at raster resolution — crescent moon and stars for one door, sun with rays for the other, drawn as transparent overlays so the wood door shows through.

Then I'm sketching the rug design: a deep wine background with gold border and indigo inner field, diamond patterning along the edges, and a central magic circle with rings, a hexagram, and rune tick marks, sized at 768x384. I'm also starting on a transparent circular emblem icon.

For the orb texture I'm drawing an equirectangular gradient from top to bottom color with lighter swirl strokes and dots to suggest surface detail. The spark texture is a simple four-point star path with a small circle, white so it can be tinted later. I'm tallying up the twelve total textures needed—sky, sparkles, door variants, rug, emblem, runes, orb pieces, and spark—confirming the count matches, then noting a potential pitfall with how the glow effect gets applied across textured planes.

Now I'm thinking through how glow should only trigger for flat or textured parts, not paint materials, and how parts sharing the same flat color can share a material while glow strength gets applied individually. I'm defining grain-based wood materials using a cel-shading helper, setting up vertical and horizontal grain variants plus a darker wood tone, and starting a gold material definition.

Adding stone material and import list...

For the dais itself, I'm planning two stacked slabs for a stepped platform look—a larger lower slab and a slightly smaller upper one—using a scaled stone paint for the cel shading.

Now I'm thinking through lathe profiles for rotational shapes: the outline needs to be a closed loop starting and ending at the central axis with non-negative x coordinates, so a simple pedestal shape would trace from the base up to the top radius and back to center. I'm sketching a helper function that converts a simpler point list into that closed axis-to-axis loop automatically.

I also want a `turn` function that handles the axis prefixing/suffixing logic with adjustable smoothness and segment count, using fewer segments for low-poly small objects. For other decorative elements like crown trim and gold shelf edges, I'll reuse basic box sweeps, and for stars I'm defining a function that alternates outer and inner radius points with sharp corners, then extrudes that 2D outline along the thickness axis facing the viewer.

Now I'm designing the floating orb above the book: a small glowing cyan sphere wrapped in three thin rotating gold torus rings, plus scattered sparkle particles around it. I'm also working out the `cards` function signature, where frames are built from a position and direction, and flow/lean parameters control how the card orientation flattens against a surface versus standing upright facing the camera.

Starting to write the import statements and setting up the builder utilities...

Defining colors and palettes...

Adding a sphere helper function and sorting out the options parameter typing so it accepts flexible extra properties without strict TypeScript errors.

Now I'm writing a lathe helper that builds a profile by mirroring points around the axis, closing the top and bottom automatically, and handling the edge case where duplicate points get silently dropped.

I'm also setting up a glow wrapper function and a sparkle collection system that groups spark points by key, then at the end renders each group as a batch of glowing cards oriented with a frame function, sized and colored per group.

Now I'm writing a book-building function that places front/back covers and spine as box geometries positioned relative to a center point and orientation quaternion.

Still working out book rotations...

Now I'm writing a lean() helper that computes the center position and rotation for a book tilted at an angle, using the tilt angle to offset x and y based on the book's thickness and height, then applying a z-rotation so the book leans against something while sitting at the right depth.

I'm also setting up a row() function that places a series of books side by side along x, incrementing by each book's thickness with spacing, and planning a mk() generator that randomizes book thickness, height, and depth so rows look naturally varied.

For row C1, I'm checking whether 9 generated books fit the compartment width—if the average thickness overflows, I need to drop to 8 books and add a couple of leaning books at an angle to fill the remaining gap, computing their contact points based on tilt angle and height.

With 8 books the row ends safely within the compartment, leaving room for the ball at roughly 0.14, so I'm defining a thickness range per book (around 0.04 to 0.065) that keeps the total width under the boundary while still looking varied.

Now I'm writing a helper function for drawing a scroll — a cylinder body with a gold-capped core and an optional decorative band positioned slightly offset along its axis.

I'm planning a pyramid arrangement of six scrolls stacked in rows, computing spacing based on radius so they nestle together, and picking parchment color variants with accent bands for variety. Next I'm starting a candle-drawing function...

Adding drip and wick details...

I'll start the lathe profile from a nonzero x to avoid dedupe issues, keeping the low-poly teardrop flame look with six segments. Now I'm shaping the candlestick holder and orb stand profiles, building gold lathe shapes for the base, stem, and cup.

Still writing lathe geometry...

Still shaping the hourglass bulbs...

Now I'm defining helper objects for the scene: a potion bottle with a glowing lathe shape, brown cork, and thin neck band; and a skull with a scaled cranium sphere, jaw box, and glowing purple eye sockets.

I'm also working out an open book shape, positioning cover boards and tilted page boxes so the inner edges rise correctly with rotation.

Now I'm adding rune texture planes on the pages, figuring out the Euler rotation order needed to make them face upward while matching the page tilt.

Adding the orbiting ring and floating orb above the scene, then designing a scroll urn with a lathed vase profile in deep teal ceramic with a gold rim, and placing five scrolls standing inside at varied offsets, tilts, and lengths.

Still placing props...

Adding the hanging stars next: thin rod cylinders dropping from the ceiling underside with small glowing gold star extrusions at the ends, plus a small purple orb pedestal near C3. Now I'm laying out C3's contents along the x-axis—skull and candle, a row of books, then an open book positioned further along.

For the right side of C3, I'm placing a floating orb above the open book, then a vase, a small orb stand with a cup, and considering a leaning book against the wall—adjusting positions slightly to avoid overlaps between the orb, vase, and leaning book. I'm nudging the orb to x=0.47 to keep spacing clean, then moving on to work out the C2 arrangement.

Now I'm laying out the stack starting at x=-0.5 with three lying books topped by a candlestick, keeping total height under the 0.48 limit. Then I'm adding six vertical books from x=-0.36, an hourglass, two potions (green and pink), followed by more vertical books and a leaning book near the wall—working through the x-coordinates to make sure everything fits without overlapping.

Now I'm adding gold trim strips along the front of each shelf board, positioning them at the board centers along the z-axis.

I realize I need to clean up my shelf-level naming: LV holds the vertical positions [0.66, 1.18, 1.70, 2.22], with board tops T1-T3 computed as Y0+LV[i]+0.02 for the first three levels, and the ceiling board using LV[3]. The cabinet sits between the plinth top and these shelf levels, so I'm re-mapping which compartment corresponds to which board index to keep the geometry consistent.

Door height comes out to 0.48 centered at Y0+0.39, and side panels run the full height to Y0+2.24 with their outer edges at ±0.71. The top board overhangs to span the full width of 1.56 while the shelf boards below are narrower at 1.34, and I'm sizing the plinth as 1.56 x 0.14 x 0.46 before adding a gold toe-kick strip on top of it.

Adding gem studs and feet positions, checking pillar and plinth width alignment at ±0.76/±0.78, and sizing the back sky plane to fit within the compartment boards.

Now I'm placing the crown pieces, noting the back is hidden so it doesn't need detail, and applying dark wood grain paint via the extrude's point coordinates. For the emblem, I'm positioning a glowing circle plane at the crown's front face, using a cropped texture disc to represent the dark emblem centered on the crown.

Checking the emblem position at center y = CTOP+0.14: comparing crown height at x=0 (0.35) versus x=±0.15 (about 0.27), I size the emblem radius to 0.13 and center at y=.16 so its top edge (0.29) stays safely under the crown's curve. I'm adding a thin gold torus ring around the emblem to frame it, sized slightly larger than the emblem radius and positioned at the same depth facing forward. Now I'm sketching the eave trim as a thin box running along the top edge.

I should rotate the outline by +90° so the opening faces upward like a cup, which moves the inner circle center to sit above the arc's midpoint — the orb then rests inside that cup near the inner center. I'm computing the actual outer and inner arc points now with R=0.12 and φ=48°, stepping through angles to build the point list.

Checking for duplicate points where outer and inner arcs meet at the endpoints — these coincide exactly, so I'm dropping the repeated points at both the join and the closing point to avoid a degenerate outline.

I'm sketching a helper for generating a star shape by alternating outer and inner radius points around a rotation starting at the top, marking each vertex as sharp.

Now I'm positioning small gold stars on the crown face, computing their y-coordinates from the crown profile curve at given x positions so they sit nicely along the curved edges, placing pairs symmetrically at roughly (±0.35, 0.1) and (±0.58, 0.07) with a small radius, plus adding a glow element.

For the pillars, I'm adding finials on top as already planned, skipping extra front trim strips, and instead adding glowing rune-strip planes on each side panel (facing outward at ±x) paired with gold trim rectangles, sized about 0.3 by 0.4 and positioned near the upper portion of the pillar with moderate glow intensity.

Now I'm scattering floor clutter: on the left, a tilted pile of four books at varied yaw angles with a melted cream candle on top, and possibly a leaning scroll; on the right, a stone saucer holding a cluster of three candles of different heights and radii, built as a lathed profile shape.

I'm also sketching a small cluster of five-sided crystal spikes in cyan and lilac tones, positioning them off to the front-left and front-right of the scene with a glow effect applied to each mesh.

I'm adding floor sparkle accents and considering small gold lamp posts at the front corners of the dais, each topped with a glowing orb to frame the composition symmetrically.

Tallying up the approximate part counts—shelves, books, scrolls, candles, and sparkle meshes—to get a rough sense of total scene complexity, landing around 350 parts. I confirm texture and quaternion options are consistent, randomness ordering is deterministic, and the joint root is positioned correctly.

Writing the star field SVG generation loop...

Still writing SVG code...

Designing spine variants with gold accent lines and decorative motifs...

I'll fill the inner panel with a deep indigo so the gold moon shape glows against it, matching the sun door treatment with warm gold rays on the same dark base, then move on to composing the rug with a maroon background, gold border frame, and nested inner rectangles.
